hunks.baseline: The underground prison beneath the Sichuan Tang Clan was a dark, damp place by nature.
hunks.sol: The underground prison beneath the Sichuan Tang Clan was dark and damp by nature.

hunks.baseline: The torches hanging here and there gave off less light than fireflies, and the floor was covered in stagnant water of unknown origin that made squelching sounds whenever anyone walked across it.
hunks.sol: The few torches spaced along the walls gave off less light than fireflies, and the floor was covered in stagnant water of unknown origin that squelched underfoot.

hunks.baseline: “What a foul smell. Even if this is a prison, how can they lock people up in a place like this?”
hunks.sol: “What a foul smell. Prison or not, how can they lock people up in a place like this?”

hunks.baseline: “People? This is a place for raising beasts. Haven’t you heard that the Sichuan Tang Clan captured the fiends of the Great Faction War and subjected them to all kinds of torture? It’s no surprise that a place like this exists.”
hunks.sol: “People? This is where they keep beasts. Haven’t you heard that the Sichuan Tang Clan captured fiends from the Great Faction War and subjected them to every torture imaginable? A place like this should hardly surprise you.”

hunks.baseline: There were two voices, but several sets of footsteps.
hunks.sol: There were two voices, but far more sets of footsteps.

hunks.baseline: I quietly raised my Qi Sense and counted them.
hunks.sol: I quietly extended my Qi Sense and counted them.

hunks.baseline: The two men at the front, whom I assumed to be the leaders of the group, continued talking.
hunks.sol: The two men at the front, presumably the group’s leaders, continued their conversation.

hunks.baseline: “But why can’t I see any prisoners? There are only iron bars, and the cells are empty.”
hunks.sol: “But where are all the prisoners? There are bars everywhere, but the cells are empty.”

hunks.baseline: “Everyone imprisoned here is an old monster from the Great Faction War. It wouldn’t be strange if they had died long ago. Especially after being tortured in a place like this.”
hunks.sol: “Everyone imprisoned here is an old monster from the days of the Great Faction War. It wouldn’t be strange if they’d died long ago, especially after being tortured in a place like this.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s true.”
hunks.sol: “Fair point.”

hunks.baseline: It was true that many of the first-generation inmates of the underground prison had already gone to the other world, but more than ten prisoners still remained here.
hunks.sol: Many of the underground prison’s original residents had indeed passed on to the next world, but more than ten prisoners still remained.

hunks.baseline: What they had failed to anticipate was that someone unseen had used Pressure-Point Strike on the prisoners and moved them elsewhere.
hunks.sol: What they could not have guessed was that someone lurking out of sight had struck the prisoners’ pressure points and moved them elsewhere.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “I can’t see even a single ant. Wouldn’t it be better to go back upstairs and kill at least one more person?”
hunks.sol: “There isn’t so much as an ant down here. Wouldn’t we be better off going back upstairs and killing another person or two?”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t think we’ve even searched half the place yet.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t think we’ve searched even half the place yet.”

hunks.baseline: “Since you mention it, what could possibly be further in? The others will come and search every corner anyway.”
hunks.sol: “Now that you mention it, what could there possibly be farther in? The others will come through and search every last corner anyway.”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t talk nonsense. Have you forgotten the order given by the Lord of Heaven? What if someone of the Tang Clan’s bloodline is hiding here…?”
hunks.sol: “Don’t be ridiculous. Have you forgotten the Lord of Heaven’s command? What if someone of the Tang bloodline is hiding down here…?”

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “No one would be stupid enough to hide in an underground prison. The battle isn’t even over yet, so why would they hide here? I could understand trying to break through the encirclement and escape, but this?”
hunks.sol: “No one but a complete idiot would hide in an underground prison. The battle isn’t even over yet, so why would anyone come down here? Trying to break through the encirclement and flee would make more sense.”

hunks.baseline: The man let out a low groan, then spoke in a firm voice.
hunks.sol: The man pondered for a moment, then answered firmly.

hunks.baseline: “Impossible. We serve the solemn command of the revered Lord of Heaven. With the Demon Lord leading by example, do you intend to handle your duty carelessly?”
hunks.sol: “No. We have been entrusted with the revered Lord of Heaven’s command. The Demon Lord himself is leading by example, yet you intend to shirk your duty?”

hunks.baseline: “Phew. Damn it.”
hunks.sol: “Damn it.”

hunks.baseline: The Dark Heaven martial artist whose face I did not know had no idea that his fate had been decided by those words.
hunks.sol: That Dark Heaven martial artist had no idea his fate had just been sealed by those words.

hunks.baseline: The other man grumbled at his firm tone.
hunks.sol: At his firm response, the other man grumbled.

hunks.baseline: “You really need to show some flexibility. If you keep living so rigidly, you’ll die before your time.”
hunks.sol: “You ought to learn some flexibility. Keep living like such a stickler and you’ll die before your time.”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t say such unlucky things. I’ll live longer than you, who always do everything half-assed, so don’t worry.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t say such ill-omened things. I’ll live longer than someone who half-asses everything like you, so worry about yourself.”

hunks.baseline: “Want to bet on it?”
hunks.sol: “Want to bet?”

hunks.baseline: “Fine. It’s not as if I can’t—”
hunks.sol: “Fine. Why wouldn’t I—”

hunks.baseline: To give you the conclusion first, the longevity bet between the two men ended with the one who did everything half-assed winning.
hunks.sol: Long story short, the man who half-assed everything won their bet over who would live longer.

hunks.baseline: Of course, the difference between their deaths amounted to no more than a moment.
hunks.sol: Though only by a fraction of a second.

hunks.baseline: Thrust!
hunks.sol: Shnk!

hunks.baseline: It was a perfect surprise attack.
hunks.sol: It was a perfect ambush.

hunks.baseline: In the maze-like corridor, I had been waiting in the darkness with my presence concealed. The instant I drove the dagger in my left hand into one man’s eye, I swung the sword in my right.
hunks.sol: I had concealed my presence and waited in the darkness of the maze-like passage. The instant I drove the dagger in my left hand into one man’s eye, I swung the sword in my right.

hunks.baseline: The blade, which I had coated in mud beforehand to keep it from reflecting light, cleaved through flesh and bone.
hunks.sol: I had smeared mud over the blade beforehand to keep it from catching the light. It sheared through flesh and bone.

hunks.baseline: The two Peak masters died without even managing to scream. Their bodies collapsed like rotten logs.
hunks.sol: The two Peak masters died without so much as a scream, collapsing like rotten logs.

hunks.baseline: The black-robed men, suddenly drenched in blood and filthy water, stared back and forth between the bodies of their leaders and me with vacant eyes.
hunks.sol: Suddenly drenched in blood and filthy water, the black-robed men stared blankly between their leaders’ bodies and me.

hunks.baseline: “W-What is…?”
hunks.sol: “W-What…?”

hunks.baseline: There were thirteen left.
hunks.sol: Thirteen left.

hunks.baseline: I answered by swinging my sword.
Once again, accompanied by a dreadful sound of flesh being torn, a severed head rose into the air.
hunks.sol: Instead of answering, I swung my sword again. With another grisly sound of parting flesh, a severed head flew into the air.

hunks.baseline: “Twelve now.”
hunks.sol: “Twelve.”

hunks.baseline: An emotion appeared in their previously empty eyes.
hunks.sol: A single emotion surfaced in their vacant eyes.

hunks.baseline: It was fear.
hunks.sol: Fear.

hunks.baseline: “You’re trapped, right? The layout here is kind of fucked up. Apparently, they built it this way in case any prisoners tried to escape.”
hunks.sol: “Dead end, huh? The layout down here is pretty fucked up. Apparently, they built it this way in case anyone tried to escape.”

hunks.baseline: I walked toward the rat cornered at the end of the passage.
hunks.sol: I walked toward the rat trapped at the end of the passage.

hunks.baseline: Of course, he was far too large to actually be called a rat. Despite his size, however, he had been the quickest of them all to run away, perhaps because he was such a coward.
hunks.sol: Granted, he was rather large for a rat. But despite his size, he had been the first to run. Apparently, he was a coward.

hunks.baseline: “All right. Let’s go to hell and join your friends.”
hunks.sol: “All right. Time to join your friends in hell.”

hunks.baseline: “You crazy bastard. So it’s romance when you do it, but adultery when I do?”
hunks.sol: “You crazy bastard. When you do it, it’s romance, but when I do it, it’s adultery?”

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man dropped to his knees, his face gone deathly pale. He was still holding a weapon, but he already knew perfectly well that it would do him no good against me.
hunks.sol: The black-robed man dropped to his knees, his face deathly pale. He still had his weapon in hand, but by now he knew perfectly well that it was useless against me.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: In the end, the method he chose was to beg for his life.
hunks.sol: In the end, he resorted to begging for his life.

hunks.baseline: Without hesitation, I broke the black-robed man’s neck. His head tilted at an unnatural angle, his tongue hanging from his mouth.
hunks.sol: I snapped the black-robed man’s neck without hesitation. His tongue lolled out as his head tilted at an unnatural angle.

hunks.baseline: Instant death. No doubt about it.
hunks.sol: Instant death. No question.

hunks.baseline: “You people always make me do things twice. You weren’t going to get very far anyway.”
hunks.sol: “You people always make me do the same job twice. It’s not like you were going to get far.”

hunks.baseline: With a sigh, I hoisted him over my shoulder and started walking back the way I had come. It did not take long to return to the place where I had launched my first surprise attack.
hunks.sol: With a sigh, I slung him over my shoulder and retraced my steps. It did not take long to return to the site of my initial ambush.

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man had not been able to run very far in the first place, and I had grown familiar with the underground prison’s labyrinthine structure over the past ten days.
hunks.sol: The man had not made it very far, and over the past ten days I had become familiar with the underground prison’s labyrinthine layout.

hunks.baseline: “Bastards. What the hell are you crawling all the way in here for? Is there something to eat?”
hunks.sol: “Fucking bastards. What scraps are there to scavenge all the way down here?”

hunks.baseline: This was the second time black-robed men had infiltrated the underground prison.
hunks.sol: This was the second time the black-robed men had infiltrated the underground prison.

hunks.baseline: About thirty minutes earlier, seven of them had entered first, and I had taken care of every last one.
hunks.sol: About thirty minutes ago, seven of them had come in. I had killed every last one.

hunks.baseline: I had helped the Sichuan Tang Clan reduce the enemy’s numbers, but I did not feel the slightest bit happy about it. I knew what their intrusion meant.
hunks.sol: I had helped thin the enemy’s ranks for the Sichuan Tang Clan, but I could not feel happy about it. I knew what their presence meant.

hunks.baseline: The underground prison was located on the outskirts of the Tang Clan’s Inner Hall. That meant the Outer Hall, which could be considered the front line, had already been breached.
hunks.sol: The underground prison stood on the outskirts of the Tang Clan’s Inner Hall. If the enemy had reached this place, then the Outer Hall—the front line—had already fallen.

hunks.baseline: I shook my head at the ominous thought that suddenly crossed my mind.
hunks.sol: I shook my head as an ominous thought flashed through my mind.

hunks.baseline: *No way. Even if you dropped Cheongpung into the middle of hell, he’d be the kind of guy who came back alive.*
hunks.sol: No. Cheongpung was the sort of guy who could be dropped into the middle of hell and still come back alive.

hunks.baseline: No. He had to be.
hunks.sol: He had to be.

hunks.baseline: *Damn it. If only I could at least log out. Then there’d be a little hope.*
hunks.sol: *Damn it. If I could at least log out, we might have a chance.*

hunks.baseline: I had wondered if it might work, but as expected, it did not.
hunks.sol: I had held out some hope, but no such luck.

hunks.baseline: The System had blocked the Logout function as soon as the Quest began.
hunks.sol: The System had disabled Logout the instant the Quest began.

hunks.baseline: Besides, even if Logout suddenly became available right now, I could not recklessly return.
hunks.sol: Besides, even if Logout suddenly became available, I could not risk returning to the modern world.

hunks.baseline: There had already been two intrusions in the past thirty minutes. If the enemy stormed in while I was spending even a short time in the modern world…
hunks.sol: The enemy had already broken in twice within the past thirty minutes. If they stormed the place while I was gone, even briefly…

hunks.baseline: *Not only me, but Jeok Cheongang and the Divine Physician would be finished.*
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang, the Divine Physician, and I would all be finished.

hunks.baseline: *I have no choice but to stop them here.*
hunks.sol: *I have no choice. I have to stop them here.*

hunks.baseline: They had numbers on their side, while I was alone.
hunks.sol: They had numbers. I was alone.

hunks.baseline: So, just as before, I needed to make the most of surprise attacks and conserve my strength in case of an emergency.
hunks.sol: I needed to keep making the most of ambushes, as I had just done, while conserving my strength for an emergency.

hunks.baseline: *If they come in and find corpses scattered everywhere, it’ll all be for nothing.*
hunks.sol: *The whole plan goes to hell if they walk in and find corpses everywhere.*

hunks.baseline: I began moving the bodies lying around one by one.
hunks.sol: I began moving the scattered bodies one by one.

hunks.baseline: The place I had designated as a temporary morgue was the deepest, darkest part of the underground prison.
hunks.sol: The place I had chosen as my temporary morgue lay in the deepest, darkest reaches of the underground prison.

hunks.baseline: “It’s been a while. Has it been about half an hour since I last saw you?”
hunks.sol: “Long time no see. What’s it been, half an hour?”

hunks.baseline: “I brought some new friends so you wouldn’t be lonely.”
hunks.sol: “I brought you some new friends so you wouldn’t get lonely.”

hunks.baseline: At the center of the prison, where not a single ray of light reached, an old man covered in dangling restraints glared at me with blazing eyes.
hunks.sol: At the center of the prison, where not a single ray of light could reach, an old man festooned with restraints glared at me with blazing eyes.

hunks.baseline: He was the Heavenly Power Demon.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon.

hunks.baseline: “What? Got something to say?”
hunks.sol: “What?”

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “What are you going to do by glaring at me like that? If you have something to say, go ahead.”
hunks.sol: “What are you going to do, glare me to death? If you’ve got something to say, say it.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, right. The pressure points.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, right. Your pressure points.”

hunks.baseline: I had struck his Paralysis Acupoint and Mute Acupoint, so naturally he had been unable to say anything.
hunks.sol: I had struck his Paralysis Acupoint and Mute Acupoint, so of course he could not speak.

hunks.baseline: I walked over and unsealed his acupoints. Only then did his angry voice burst out.
hunks.sol: I walked over and released them. His furious voice immediately burst out.

hunks.baseline: “Then why the hell are you moving those corpses here?”
hunks.sol: “I can see that! Why the hell are you bringing them here?”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t shout. If you raise your voice one more time, I might strike a lethal acupoint instead of your Mute Acupoint.”
hunks.sol: “Keep your voice down. Shout one more time and I might strike a lethal acupoint instead of your Mute Acupoint.”

hunks.baseline: Good. He was quiet now.
hunks.sol: Much better.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: Leaving the silenced Heavenly Power Demon behind, I began stacking the bodies I had brought into the prison.
hunks.sol: Leaving the now-silent Heavenly Power Demon behind me, I began neatly stacking the bodies inside the cell.

hunks.baseline: Thump. Rumble-rumble.
hunks.sol: Thump. Roll…

hunks.baseline: “Could you pick up that head over there?”
hunks.sol: “Could you pick up that head?”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, right. You’re wearing restraints.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, right. You’re in restraints.”

hunks.baseline: “Huff. Huff.”
hunks.sol: “Huff! Huff!”

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon’s face reddened as he snorted angrily. Even so, he seemed unwilling to have me strike a lethal acupoint, because he barely managed to suppress the shout rising to his throat.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon’s face flushed crimson as he snorted through his nose. Still, he apparently had no desire to get struck in a lethal acupoint, because he just barely swallowed the shout rising in his throat.

hunks.baseline: “What the hell is wrong with you…?”
hunks.sol: “What in the world is wrong with you…?”

hunks.baseline: “What? Did you have something to say?”
hunks.sol: “What? Something you want to say?”

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon had remained silent despite my efforts to coax information out of him for the past several days.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon had refused to utter a word despite my efforts to coax information out of him over the past several days.

hunks.baseline: A man who must have seen enough corpses during the Great Faction War to be sick of them had to have a reason for whining now. Having struck the mark, I watched him stammer.
hunks.sol: A man who had seen enough corpses during the Great Faction War to last a lifetime would not be complaining now without a reason. My suspicion had clearly hit the mark, and he began to stammer.

hunks.baseline: “N-No. Nothing.”
hunks.sol: “N-No.”

hunks.baseline: “Then we’re done here.”
hunks.sol: “Then we’re done.”

hunks.baseline: “W-Wait. Wait just a moment.”
hunks.sol: “W-Wait. Wait a moment.”

hunks.baseline: “This is your last chance. If you have something to say, say it quickly.”
hunks.sol: “Last chance. If you have something to say, spit it out.”

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon moved his lips for a while before letting out a deep sigh.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon’s lips worked silently for a moment before he let out a deep sigh.

hunks.baseline: “Then what exactly are these corpses?”
hunks.sol: “Then what are these corpses?”

hunks.baseline: He asked as if it were nothing important, but the way he cautiously watched my expression showed that this was what he had really been curious about.
hunks.sol: He tried to sound unconcerned, but the way he studied my expression made it obvious that this was what he had really wanted to ask.

hunks.baseline: For the past several decades, the only person who had visited the prison had been Old Man Gung, carrying torture implements. It was understandable that he would be curious after nearly twenty naked corpses had suddenly been piled up here.
hunks.sol: For the past several decades, his only visitor had been Old Man Gung bearing instruments of torture. Now nearly twenty naked corpses had suddenly been piled in front of him. Of course he was curious.

hunks.baseline: “Has some disaster befallen the Tang Clan?”
hunks.sol: “Has some calamity befallen the Tang Clan?”

hunks.baseline: “It has.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah.”

hunks.baseline: I added one brief sentence.
hunks.sol: I added a brief explanation.

hunks.baseline: It was the same expression he had worn a few days ago.
hunks.sol: It was the same expression I had seen on his face a few days ago.

hunks.baseline: I ignored the Heavenly Power Demon, who had frozen at the words *Dark Heaven*, and continued.
hunks.sol: Pretending not to notice how the words *Dark Heaven* had made the Heavenly Power Demon freeze, I continued.

hunks.baseline: “The Outer Hall has already been breached, and a fierce battle is probably still raging in the Inner Hall. The battle is going worse than expected.”
hunks.sol: “The Outer Hall has already been breached. There’s probably a fierce battle raging in the Inner Hall as we speak. Things are going worse than expected.”

hunks.baseline: “You must have interrogated the prisoners as well. I’m asking who is leading those bastards.”
hunks.sol: “You must have interrogated your captives. This old man is asking who leads them.”

hunks.baseline: “You’re sharper than I expected.”
hunks.sol: “Pretty sharp.”

hunks.baseline: I had already squeezed information out of one of the seven who first entered the prison.
hunks.sol: I had interrogated one of the seven men from the first incursion.

hunks.baseline: He had been so terrified that he severed his own heart meridian and killed himself, so I had not learned much. But I had managed to hear one man’s title.
hunks.sol: He had been terrified, but he severed his own heart meridian and killed himself before I could learn much. Still, I had managed to get one man’s title from him.

hunks.baseline: Just four words.
hunks.sol: Four words.

hunks.baseline: But the effect they had on the Heavenly Power Demon was enormous.
hunks.sol: But their effect on the Heavenly Power Demon was tremendous.

hunks.baseline: The old man, who had always hung from his restraints with a gaunt body reduced to skin and bones, yanked at the chains as if he might leap out of the prison at any moment.
hunks.sol: The old man had always hung limply from his restraints, his gaunt body reduced to skin and bone. Now he hauled at the chains as though he might tear himself free at any moment.

hunks.baseline: “I-Is he still alive? Then what about the Cult Leader? What happened to the Cult Leader?”
hunks.sol: “I-Is he still alive? Then the Cult Leader! What happened to the Cult Leader?”

hunks.baseline: What was wrong with this old man all of a sudden?
hunks.sol: What the hell was wrong with this old man all of a sudden?

hunks.baseline: Taken aback, I answered.
hunks.sol: Caught off guard, I answered.

hunks.baseline: “……At this hour? He’s probably eating breakfast.”
hunks.sol: “…At this hour? He’s probably eating breakfast.”

hunks.baseline: It was my first time hearing the title Western Heaven Demon Lord, so how would I know what had happened to the Demonic Cult’s Cult Leader? It was not as if the Demonic Cult had an official Twitter account.
hunks.sol: This was the first time I had ever heard the title Western Heaven Demon Lord. How the hell would I know what the Demonic Cult’s Cult Leader was doing? It wasn’t as if the Demonic Cult had an official Twitter account.

hunks.baseline: “So it finally came to this. In the end, it came to this! Ha-ha… Ha-ha-ha!”
hunks.sol: “So it has finally come to this. In the end… it has come to this. Ha. Ha-ha-ha!”

hunks.baseline: After muttering incomprehensible words, the Heavenly Power Demon began laughing like a man who had lost his mind.
hunks.sol: After babbling words I could not understand, the Heavenly Power Demon began laughing like a man who had lost his mind.

hunks.baseline: I stared at him for a moment, then suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: I watched him for a moment, then spoke.

hunks.baseline: “Spill it now. What’s the relationship between the Demonic Cult and Dark Heaven? And what the fuck kind of bastard is this Western Heaven Demon Lord?”
hunks.sol: “Spill it. What’s the connection between the Demonic Cult and Dark Heaven? And what kind of fucking bastard is this Western Heaven Demon Lord?”

hunks.baseline: The laughter that had echoed throughout the prison abruptly stopped.
hunks.sol: The laughter echoing through the prison abruptly stopped.

hunks.baseline: The Heavenly Power Demon’s empty gaze turned toward me.
hunks.sol: The Heavenly Power Demon’s hollow gaze settled on me.

hunks.baseline: “He—the man you call the Western Heaven Demon Lord—was one of the four Protectors of the Divine Cult. He served the Cult Leader from closer than anyone else…and he was the one who led him astray.”
hunks.sol: “He—the man you call the Western Heaven Demon Lord—was one of the Divine Cult’s four Protectors. He served closer to the Cult Leader than anyone…and led him astray.”

hunks.baseline: “One day, he began calling himself the Western Heaven Demon Lord. That was the beginning of everything. And in the end, it came to this. It finally came to this. Ha-ha… Hahahaha!”
hunks.sol: “One day, he began calling himself the Western Heaven Demon Lord. That was the beginning of everything. And now it has come to this. In the end, it has come to this. Ha-ha… Hahahaha!”

hunks.baseline: At that exact moment, the Heavenly Power Demon burst into crazed laughter.
hunks.sol: At that very moment, the Heavenly Power Demon erupted into crazed laughter.

hunks.baseline: Along with a tremendous roar from far away, the underground prison trembled.
hunks.sol: A tremendous roar sounded in the distance, and the underground prison shook.
